[1/3] Seed the network generator so each run grows a varied side-subnet layer of contract hosts

impact_assessment.why: network.py advertises a network generated from the seed but never uses its rng, so every run has the identical seven-host grid and much of the advertised replay/contract variety is absent.
impact_assessment.benefits: Distinct side hosts, routes, loot and contract targets per seed while the campaign spine stays fixed; the documented --seed guarantee becomes true.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: canonical node IDs/IPs/files and save schema stay unchanged; dependency: standard library only; concurrency: generation is local to engine construction; state: side hosts are plain Nodes serialized with the existing schema.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add only LOCKED side hosts beside the fixed spine, keep anchors reciprocal, prove same-seed determinism and cross-seed variation, and run the full project check before commit.

[1/3] Give the Web Cyberdeck the terminal's atomic save/load parity

impact_assessment.why: The Web Cyberdeck is the default launcher but holds the run only in server memory: closing the server loses the run, while the terminal already has crash-safe save/load. The server persists career stats but never the run.
impact_assessment.benefits: Players can bank a long run from the browser, resume the exact seeded state including pending puzzles and RNG, and see a CONTINUE action only when a save exists.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: storage schema and CLI semantics unchanged; dependency: none; concurrency: save/load run under the existing session lock; state: load replaces the session engine and clears the transient puzzle UI.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Reuse SaveManager, refuse terminal saves, expose has_save in the state payload, add API and session tests, and run the full project gate.

[1/6] Add autosave and three named save slots across terminal and Web Cyberdeck

impact_assessment.why: ADR-024 gave both interfaces one manual save file; players still lose progress if they forget to save and cannot keep more than one run.
impact_assessment.benefits: Crash-safe progress recovery, parallel runs, and a load menu that works in both interfaces without changing the campaign.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: save schema and load semantics shared by CLI, web and storage; dependency: none; concurrency: single-user local files with atomic writes; state: existing single savegame.json must keep loading and terminal anti-replay must survive.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Keep slot 1 mapped to the legacy files, add explicit auto/manual ownership metadata, migrate on read, and cover legacy load, slot isolation and settlement cleanup with failing-first tests.
